extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalists, and news homepage designers/editors
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and mechanisms by which news coverage makes issues salient and primes evaluation — i.e., which stories a news homepage should promote to shape what viewers consider important and the criteria they use to judge leaders. Useful for editors designing prominence (position, length, visuals, repetition) on homepages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues that received extended coverage became more important to viewers; issues that were ignored lost credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize which issues to bring to public attention: frequency and prominence of coverage shift perceived importance. Example: repeated coverage of an issue across nights/outlets increases salience. Scoring notes: measure presence/absence and relative attention compared to other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priming
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues prominent in the news stream become evaluation criteria citizens use when judging leaders (e.g., economic stories make viewers judge the president on the economy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting certain topics changes which performance dimensions the public uses to evaluate officials. Editors should recognize that topic choice shapes political accountability, not just information. Evaluate by tracking subsequent changes in issue-based evaluations of leaders after coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition Confers Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The same story across nights/outlets builds salience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat stories across time and channels to raise issue salience. On homepages, replicating a story across sections or featuring it repeatedly increases perceived importance. Anti-pattern: one-off placement is less likely to move public priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead-Story Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening segment (lead story) of a broadcast carries amplified weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top/front placement on a homepage confers extra salience beyond mere presence. Scoring: rank positions (lead/top slot) as higher impact than downstream slots; prioritize which stories to put first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length Premium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer treatments or deeper packages (long-form pieces, extended blocks) increase salience relative to short mentions. On homepages, link to in-depth pieces or expanded coverage to signal importance; brief wire-copy is lower impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Treatment Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories with strong visuals achieve disproportionate salience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prominent images, video, and striking visuals to amplify attention. Homepage design should weight items with larger images or video players more heavily. Anti-pattern: text-only small links are less likely to prime public concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-Relevant Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories on issues that connect to current officeholders' performance get extra newsworthiness because they directly bear on political accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories that can be linked to officials' credit or blame; these are more likely to influence evaluations of leaders. Evaluate by whether a story can be framed as bearing on executive or legislative performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue-Coupling
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that can be coupled to other prominent themes (e.g., a domestic crime story coupled to ongoing crime-policy debate) gain coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek or highlight angles that link a story to larger, ongoing themes to increase its perceived importance. On homepages, cross-linking and thematic packages strengthen coupling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit/Blame Hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that present clear opportunities to credit or blame officials gain coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify narratives or facts within stories that make attribution straightforward; such hooks increase editorial incentive to feature the story. For evaluation, note whether coverage includes actors to be credited/blamed.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Personal Relevance (strengthens priming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priming effects are stronger when the issue has high personal relevance to viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess audience stakes: personal economic wellbeing, safety, health, etc., increase the likelihood that coverage will prime evaluations. Tailor homepage prominence for issues with demonstrated personal salience to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing Partisan Attachments (strengthens priming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing partisan attachments make blame attribution natural and strengthen priming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that partisan predispositions condition how audiences use issues to evaluate leaders; coverage may prime differently across partisan groups. Metric: audience partisan alignment and the likely direction of attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent Repetition (strengthens priming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent repetition of the story across days increases priming effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain coverage across multiple days to solidify the issue as an evaluation criterion. On homepages, maintain recurring visibility (e.g., persistent top-story placement or updates) to maximize priming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affective Tone (negative stories prime more strongly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affective tone — negative stories prime more strongly than neutral/positive ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative valence amplifies priming; consider emotional tone when assessing a story's likely influence on public evaluation. Scoring: weight negative/angry/fearful framing as higher-prime potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Source Dominance (strengthens priming)
rubrics_metrics.description: When most networks tell the same story, priming is stronger (single-source or consensus dominance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity across outlets magnifies effect; measure cross-outlet repetition and consensus to estimate priming strength. For homepages, syndicated emphasis or aligning with other major outlets increases impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizable Signals (position, length, repetition, visuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Story position, length, repetition, visuals — all measurable on a homepage — function as causal levers of public salience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these design elements as manipulable variables: top-slot placement, larger visuals, longer formats, and repeated placement can be counted and optimized. Use page analytics to quantify these signals and their correlation with audience salience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing / First-Mover Coverage Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories encountered earlier 'anchor' subsequent evaluation; first-mover coverage carries disproportionate priming weight (morning/evening news cycle matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize publishing/timing to be first on breaking items or to anchor the daily news cycle. On homepages, early-morning prominent placement or persistent fronting shapes downstream attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salience-Engineering Responsibility (normative implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: News selection is not just selection but priming — choosing which criteria voters will use to judge leaders; this makes coverage choices politically consequential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and homepage designers should be aware of the normative and political consequences of prominence choices. Consider ethical assessment and editorial accountability when promoting stories that will shape public evaluation.
